scenes.narration: May 8, 2026. HubSpot's stock fell about 20 percent in a single day. Investors were scared that AI would replace the software it sells.

title: HUBSPOT
20 YEARS OF BETS
scenes.subtitle: FROM MIT TO 288,706 CUSTOMERS
scenes.narration: And yet, that same quarter, its revenue grew 23 percent. To understand this company, we have to go back twenty years, to a university near Boston.

scenes.label: MIT
scenes.narration: Brian Halligan and Dharmesh Shah met as graduate students at MIT. They noticed something: people were getting very good at ignoring ads and cold calls.

scenes.label: DAY ONE
scenes.narration: In June 2006, they started HubSpot in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Their idea: stop interrupting people. Help them find you instead, through blogs, search and useful content.

scenes.label: IDEA LAB
scenes.narration: They gave the idea a name: inbound marketing. They even co-wrote a book about it. The bet was that a helpful blog post could beat a cold call.

scenes.label: SALES & MARKETING
scenes.narration: But first, they had to teach the world a new word. So they did what they preached. Their own blog and free content reportedly brought in their first customers.

scenes.label: CEO SUITE
scenes.narration: In 2014, HubSpot made its riskiest bet. It announced a CRM, the tool companies use to track customers, and made the core version free.

scenes.label: NEW YORK STOCK EXCHANGE
scenes.narration: One month later, HubSpot went public on the New York Stock Exchange at 25 dollars a share, raising 125 million dollars.

scenes.label: FREE USERS
scenes.narration: Why give software away? Because a free tool brings people in the door. When a business grows, it can upgrade to paid tools. Inbound, again.

scenes.label: DEAL ROOM
scenes.narration: Then, in 2024, the biggest name in tech came knocking. Reports said Google's parent company, Alphabet, was talking about buying HubSpot.
But on July 10, 2024, reports said the deal was off. The talks never reached the final checks, and HubSpot's stock fell as much as 19 percent that day.
Many companies would panic. HubSpot kept building. It added AI to its platform, including an AI agent that answers customer questions.
And the numbers kept going up. In 2025, HubSpot made 3.13 billion dollars in revenue, up 19 percent, with 288,706 customers by the end of the year.

scenes.label: SERVER ROOM
scenes.narration: Then came 2026. Fear of AI hit software stocks hard, and HubSpot's shares fell. The big question now: will AI replace HubSpot, or power it?

scenes.label: HOW TO USE IT
scenes.caption: CONTACTS → DEALS
scenes.narration: So how can you use it today? HubSpot's free CRM keeps your contacts and deals in one place, and it has no expiration date.

scenes.label: FREE PLAN
scenes.narration: It is made for small teams and freelancers who want to stay organized. If you outgrow it, paid plans add things like automation and reporting.
